# Independent review: Luna Max BibTeX Rust

## Disposition

Approve publication of the unchanged **365/386 (94.5596%)** completed result, subject to the primary publication/accounting checks. The 21 failed observations are supported implementation defects, not an infrastructure interruption or a newly identified oracle blocker. Several observations share one root cause; they are not 21 independent defects. No submitted code was executed on the host during this review. No raw evidence, eval, scoring, or publication files were changed.

Run UID: `0bb81f1b-9f97-43d3-b19f-4d32647210a6`. Raw root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/bibtex-rs-gpt-5.6-luna-max/bibtex-rs/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-luna_max/eval1/run1`. BibTeX 1.2.5, suite revision `8807848`, Codex CLI 0.153.4, gpt-5.6-luna/max, api-only. Result and pytest report agree on 365 passed, 21 failed, no skipped/errors, total 386. Generation duration 3598.109 seconds (about 60 minutes).

Read the run-eval skill, current handoff, frozen base/technical prompts, all failed report messages, the entire canonical command/message progression, relevant command outputs and source routines, and authoritative BibTeX WEB/style-guide/user-guide passages. Source is a substantial dependency-free Rust interpreter, not a stub.

## Every failed observation and its cause

Source references below are to `source/src/main.rs`; specification references are to `Evals/BibTeX/prompt/docs/authoritative/`.

### Declaration and namespace checks — 4

- `test_bst_parser_edges.py::test_duplicate_function_definition_is_rejected`: duplicate FUNCTION exits 0. Parser lines 734–744 increments the count and overwrites the same HashMap key without collision rejection. WEB `check_for_already_seen_function` (3886–3903), used by FUNCTION parsing, rejects duplicate identifiers.
- `test_bst_parser_edges.py::test_database_macro_is_not_callable_bst_function`: `MACRO {onlymacro}` is accepted as a callable expression and exits 0. Validation lines 1015 and runtime lines 1715–1716 explicitly admit/read the database macro namespace as stack-language names. WEB separates `macro_ilk` from `bst_fn_ilk`; technical requirements require unknown-function rejection rather than making a database macro callable.
- `test_errors.py::test_invalid_bst_declarations_are_rejected[crossref-redeclared]`.
- `test_errors.py::test_invalid_bst_declarations_are_rejected[sort-key-redeclared]`.

The last two exit 0 because ENTRY collects supplied fields/variables (715–724, 775–783), while validation merely unions those names with `crossref`/`sort.key$` (1012–1017). No duplicate/predefined-name check exists. WEB predefines those symbols at 8135 and 8141 and checks declaration collisions. Repeated ENTRY and READ cases do pass; the missing checks are specifically symbol-level, not complete absence of declaration validation.

### Wrong operand type defaults — 2

- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_plus_type_error_pushes_zero`: `"abc" #3 +` returns 3 instead of 0. Lines 1784–1807 substitute zero for the invalid operand, then still add the valid operand.
- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_concat_type_error_pushes_empty`: `#5 "suffix" *` retains `suffix`, producing `suffix|` instead of `|`. `pop_string` (1765–1771) individually substitutes an empty string and `*` (1826–1829) concatenates the surviving operand.

WEB `x_plus` (8417–8432) and `x_concatenate` (8470–8485) default the entire result when either operand has the wrong type. Warnings alone do not make the surviving result correct.

### Negative substring direction and alpha labels — 3 observations, one direct shared cause

- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_substring_from_end_negative_start`: `"abcdef" #-1 #3 substring$` yields `f`, not `def`.
- `test_reference_styles.py::test_reference_style_bbl_parity[refs-alpha]`: first divergence is bibliography label `ALSU6` instead of `ALSU06`; lengths 1639 vs 1649 bytes.
- `test_reference_styles.py::test_reference_style_bbl_parity[refs-edge-alpha]`: first divergence is `BMO{\etalchar{+}}2` instead of `BMO{\etalchar{+}}22`; lengths 1691 vs 1703 bytes.

`substring` lines 2652–2669 converts a negative start into an index near the end and then slices **forward**. For a negative index, the specified substring must end at that position and extend backward by the requested length. `btxhak.tex` 450–460 explicitly states this, and WEB 10822–10828 computes `sp_end` then subtracts length. Canonical `alpha.bst` 1047 and 1050 uses `#-1 #2` / `#-1 #4` to derive year components, so it loses all but the final year digit here. The report shows each first divergence, not every mismatching byte; no claim that this is the only possible difference throughout those files. The other six canonical parity cases pass, distinguishing this from the C++ run's trailing-tie parity defects.

### Name selection and grammar — 5 observations, three defects

- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_format_name_out_of_range`: asking for name 2 from `John Smith` returns empty (`|`) instead of the last scanned name (`Smith|`). Lines 2544–2547 deliberately return empty past the list end. WEB `Isolate the desired name` (9380–9400) retains the final scanned name and warns.
- `test_name_grammar_exhaustive.py::test_form1_all_lowercase_keeps_last_token` and `test_names.py::test_form1_all_lowercase`: `van de` has empty von instead of `van`. Lines 2458–2465 explicitly treat the entire trailing lowercase run as Last and return early. WEB's no-comma algorithm scans only nonlast tokens for von and retains at least the final token in Last (9683 onward, especially 9725–9735). These two tests are repeated observations of the same grammar error.
- `test_name_grammar_exhaustive.py::test_form2_leading_caps_remain_in_von` and `test_names.py::test_form2_leading_caps_remain_in_von`: `Foo van der Pol, Charles` emits von=`van der`, omitting `Foo` from von. Lines 2496–2499 put leading uppercase head tokens in Last and begin von at the first lowercase token. WEB comma-form initialization sets `von_start := 0` (9692–9708), so the expected von is `Foo van der`. Again, two tests observe one defect.

### Macro redefinition and preamble concatenation — 2

- `test_concat_and_macros.py::test_macro_concat_with_self`: successive definitions `x="start"`, then `x=x # " end"` produce `start end` rather than `end`. Lines 1189–1200 expand against the old macro map before replacing x, with no current-definition self-reference suppression. WEB `Scan a macro name` 5951–5974 suppresses a token referencing the macro currently being defined even when an older definition exists.
- `test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_preamble_concatenated`: produces `aa bb` instead of `aabb`. Line 1368 uses `preambles.join(" ")`; WEB `x_preamble` 10553–10562 appends strings directly without introducing a separator.

### Cross-reference inclusion threshold — 2

- `test_crossref_corners.py::test_crossref_parent_inclusion_threshold[1]`: emits `c0:p:2020`, expected `c0:none:2020`.
- `test_crossref_corners.py::test_crossref_parent_inclusion_threshold[2]`: emits the two children but omits `p:none:2020`.

Lines 1252–1265 select only explicitly cited entries. Lines 1300–1364 copy inherited fields but never count children to select their parent, and never remove a crossref pointer when a parent remains uncited below the threshold. `btxdoc.tex` 163–175 and WEB `min_crossrefs=2` plus filtering logic near 6580/6649 specify automatic inclusion at two cited children. The fixture puts the parent after its children, satisfying the documented order prerequisite. Inheritance itself works and must be distinguished from these selection/link-retention failures.

### Output-buffer semantics — 3

- `test_output_buffer.py::test_trailing_whitespace_removed_on_short_line`: retains spaces after `abc`.
- `test_output_buffer.py::test_whitespace_only_line_is_discarded_on_flush`: emits a spaces-only line between A and B.
- `test_output_buffer.py::test_pending_write_is_discarded_at_end_of_run`: appends unflushed `pending` after the flushed prefix.

`newline` lines 1438–1441 emits the buffer unchanged and always emits a newline; `finish` lines 1444–1449 appends pending text at EOF. WEB `output_bbl_line` 7534–7566 trims trailing whitespace and suppresses a formerly nonempty whitespace-only buffer; the main BST EOF path (3478–3483) closes files without draining the pending logical buffer. These are not missing output files or fixture setup errors.

## Oracle and public-contract caveats

The supplied summary has misleading statements around name grammar, preamble/output behavior, and related edge semantics. This was already visible in earlier BibTeX reviews. The frozen base prompt explicitly makes original authoritative sources govern whenever the summary disagrees; the primary sources above support the tested behavior. Therefore none of these 21 failures warrants a new publication hold, silent rescore, or eval mutation. The two alpha parity failures are genuine wrong year labels, not the permitted limited name-part separator relaxation.
